title: 借鉴Steam爆款玩法做小游戏，新进畅销榜小游戏《俱乐大玩家》产品分析
excerpt: 在《俱乐大玩家》中，玩家可以比上一轮自身及对手的出价还低，形成不同的策略属性。如类斗地主形式的部队称+阵营化对局、对局估值竞拍转换成对高净值藏品的溢价购买、不同难度级别、机制游戏的货币转化、对抗型角色设计等等…
text:
文/ET
数月前，Steam游戏《竞拍之王》一度成功出圈。一方面，这款竞拍游戏本身亮点颇多；另一方面，它以不到200万的制作成本、18元定价斩获数十万份销量，有较高投入产出比。近期，大梦龙途旗下小游戏《俱乐大玩家》就借鉴了《竞拍之王》的核心玩法登陆小游戏市场。近期，国内微信小游戏《俱乐大玩家》同样以《竞拍之王》的游戏玩法形式出现在小游戏市场上。
德扑式的估值竞拍有哪些不一样？
无论是《竞拍之王》还是《俱乐大玩家》，业内将这类玩法称为德扑式估值竞拍。简单来讲，《俱乐大玩家》吸纳了德州扑克的博弈、风险对抗等核心特质。原作《竞拍之王》口碑两极分化，好评玩家主要认可这套独特的游戏设计。下文将以《俱乐大玩家》为样本，对比德扑式估值竞拍与传统德州扑克的玩法差异，拆解这套玩法的核心魅力。
信息结构——从“对称”到“不对称”
《俱乐大玩家》题材原型参考美国仓库拍卖模式。去年我们曾提到国内厂商研发发行的仓库竞拍游戏《Bid Master》，累计下载达到2200万，题材和《俱乐大玩家》相近，但两款产品玩家体验差异巨大。
>注：海外版《Bid Master》中文译名同样叫《竞拍之王》，但和Steam端《竞拍之王》玩法机制完全不同，两家归属不同公司，且《Bid Master》于2024年上线。
《Bid Master》整体难度远低于《俱乐大玩家》。它的公共信息既存在对称的维度，也存在不对称的维度。对称维度下，所有玩家看到竞拍物品外观，稀有道具仅限定少数外观，玩家可以据此缩小价值判断范围；不对称维度，则体现在高价值物品分为真品、赝品。每一局内，《Bid Master》的竞拍信息，对称维度与不对称维度同时存在、作用玩家。从而构成PVPVE混合博弈。但由于《Bid Master》游戏核心玩法为单机向，所以最终仅归类于PVE类型。
德州扑克当中，全部玩家得到的公有信息数量（公共牌5张）与私有信息数量（手牌2张）处于绝对对等。对局逻辑上，玩家依靠手中两张底牌，结合公共牌组合最优牌型，多名玩家共用一副52张扑克牌。本质是玩家依托手牌与公共牌完成组合推演，属于纯多人PVP对抗。
反观《俱乐大玩家》，单局只提供部分对等信息，玩家依靠道具、角色能力进一步挖掘信息，再完成出价。每一局的公有信息规模处于动态，玩家可能在A局获知的公有信息占全局的5%，但在B局获知的公有信息占全局的20%，形成动态优劣势。动态规模的公有信息配合个人获取额外信息规模的不对等，形成显著的信息规模差异。单局层面，德扑式估值竞拍同样属于PVPVE类型。结算形式会与《Bid Master》相同：结算排序先结算哪个玩家拍得竞拍品，再结算这个玩家出价与竞拍总价的正负关，即先PVP后PVE形式的PVPVE类型。
报价节奏——从“异步”到“同步”
在《Bid Master》内，报价过程主要围绕常见的实时递增式拍卖，报价期间不存在顺序性、一致性，报价与报价之间的思考性会限制在10秒以内，玩家竞拍的过程呈现类似冲动消费的高频率提价竞标；至于德州扑克是按照庄家开始进行逐一报价，但由于每局参与人数的不同以及每局轮流作为庄家的位置不同，未进行报价的参与者在前面报价的玩家存在浮动的思考时间。而《俱乐大玩家》则是以轮次形式进行报价，玩家各自具有独立的报价思考时间，每一轮以一次性公布形式知悉。也就是说，德州扑克在报价环节是异步形式，而德扑式估值竞拍游戏在报价阶段是同步进行。报价过程上，前者知道前一个玩家做什么（高报、平报、弃权），后者并不知道。
退出机制——“中途离场”与“全程参与”
在德州扑克的游戏过程，玩家若在任意轮次选择“弃牌”时，在该局游戏中不可继续参与。而在《俱乐大玩家》内，只要没有玩家报价触发“秒拍”，所有玩家都会参与5轮竞拍，每一轮期间可由自己选择直接竞价、观望式报价、放弃报价等多种形式。同时，德州扑克的“梭哈”（全部Token投入），并不直接判该玩家获胜；而德扑估值竞拍某一玩家在这轮的报价高1.6倍第二竞拍报价时则自动判定归属。也就是说，《俱乐大玩家》存在一定程度类似桌游《血染钟楼》的“中途参与”属性，并存在德州扑克所不具备的“秒杀”属性。
风险逻辑——“火力衰减”VS“火力全开”
德州扑克类游戏，严格意义上也属于玩家主动迎接风险，背后动机在于：比赛上，最终只有一个玩家赢取其他所有玩家的Token。在单局游戏中，“加注”只会呈现递增形态，或至少持平上一轮的报价形态；而在连续对局发展规律方面，开局下注（大小盲注）会随单场比赛对局次数递增而逐步递增，即类似“吃鸡”游戏的“缩圈”设计。在《俱乐大玩家》中，玩家可以比上一轮自身及对手的出价还低，形成不同的策略属性。报价过程上，德州扑克围绕“报价即付出”，而《俱乐大玩家》在游戏结算之前，所有的报价只要不大于玩家进入游戏前的总资产都可以报价，报价过程不存在资产扣除。所以，德州扑克在单局游戏的连续报价上，属于“火力衰减”，而德扑式估值竞拍游戏，则是“火力全开”及“自由火力”的参与自由性。
主动权归属——动态的真实参与人数
在德州扑克游戏内，公共牌区域根据阶段的不同，状态从部分到全面的信息展示。《俱乐大玩家》内，所有玩家直至最终清算阶段前，都无法获知完整信息。基于这个背景下，德州扑克内，玩家资产规模是公开的，某一玩家的Token规模若比其他玩家显著低的时候，该玩家在游戏的参与主动权实质上由场中其他玩家决定，如大幅提高查看公共牌阶段的下注实现劝退，或高Token量玩家选择放弃该局胜利降低低Token玩家的获利。至于《俱乐大玩家》所有玩家陷入局部信息，玩家之间既不知道携带资产规模，彼此信息规模存在一定差异。
在纯自由报价机制下，每一轮参与玩家的规模是1-4人之间灵活波动的。如首轮可能会被秒拍，上一轮可能只有2名玩家竞价，下一轮变成4人，再下一轮可能变2-3人等等。
综合上述5个方面来看，德扑估值竞拍游戏上，存在信息不对称性、游戏参与过程玩家数灵活、参与自由性、同步参与性、“先PVP后PVE”的PVPVE属性等特质。
五个差异，是优势还是劣势？
作为玩法具有新的独到面的《俱乐大玩家》来说，毫无疑问具有好的初期吸引力。这里伴随的一个问题是：这五个特征，都是优势吗？根据Dataeye显示，《俱乐大玩家》在游戏上线初期的成绩位列微小畅销榜40名左右，中途出现轻微回落，期间一度冲入畅销榜第21位，近期出现显著回落。
投放方面，《俱乐大玩家》在8月中旬的投放规模与预热期规模相同，近期进行了一定的素材投放替换变化。从实际规模上看，《俱乐大玩家》的投放规模并不高企。从排名情况来看，投放行为具有一定的成效，但后续的排名下滑也说明投放未能形成厂商理想的病毒式裂变效应。
具体素材上，《俱乐大玩家》有不少透过AI制作的竞拍素材，竞拍场景分拍卖行、与“听泉鉴宝”直播连线、仓库竞拍等。除此之外，还有以往常见的真人配音的类直播效果型素材及“开箱”型素材。我们认为，《俱乐大玩家》的素材叙事表现上仍有成长空间，该部分思路实际上可一定程度参考海外游戏《Bid Master》的叙事表达形式。
从Steam到小游戏：五个手游化难关
整体上，我们认为《竞拍之王》类玩法分上手熟悉度、匹配机制、对局难度分布及策略空间、资产循环、长期目标等五个板块难点。本次将以《俱乐大玩家》为切入点进行观看。
新手引导粗糙，试错成本过高
《竞拍之王》类游戏上，玩家围绕货仓内的物品进行估值出价。那么，先看一下《竞拍之王》的基础设计条件。
物品总量规模海量
虽然一个仓库的物品完整属性分数量、种类、格子量、品质四类属性，但所有物品以“格子量”与“品质”锚定价值，通过每次货仓出现的物品数量、面积大小、品质浮动，形成对局差异
高价值竞拍品的设计上，基于马太效应式设计：80%-90%竞拍总价值由10%-20%竞拍品价值实现
抑制机制，货仓单场总价值存在上限规模与下限规模
严格意义上，所有玩家在每次货仓竞拍上，不会获得100%全面信息
这些基础设计机制可以看到，对于从未体验过《竞拍之王》类玩法游戏的玩家来讲，需要较高的试错成本次数。因为对于普通竞拍来说，价高者得、限时、一口价等规则较为常见，且规则与规则之间较少出现联合属性。另一方面在于“玩家会玩”与厂商视角的“玩家会玩”存在定义偏差。在玩家心中，游戏内交付的方法、窍门，能在80%场景知道什么时候应该怎么做，为“玩家会玩”；而厂商视角的“玩家会玩”，是将所有游戏方法、应对手法，直接完成提交给玩家之后，为“玩家会玩”。对于采用线性教学、用户自主驱动探索的《俱乐大玩家》来说，在该板块设计上过于粗糙。玩家完成新手教学之后，仓促进入排位赛，在试错中摸索经验。在初始的设计上，资金缺乏的玩家难以在完成新手教学之后获得连胜、资产快速积累等，游戏爽感较为滞后。
期间，若玩家该局出现红色品质商品，竞拍完成之后由于机制保护，不会进行售卖。在这阶段上，《俱乐大玩家》没有进行手游化改动。这就导致玩家虽然赢得了单场竞拍，但资产不足难以在短次数对局的竞拍环节上“舍得花”。但事实是，《俱乐大玩家》有设计每日活动、成就等多个场景提供玩家获取额外货币。于是这里的问题变成：玩家的资产滚动初期较大程度依赖于系统的日常奖励提供，但由玩家从自身胜利实现资产滚动的效益较低，又无法形成“价值>价格”的意义交付，导致缺少了高频对局驱动力。
第三个问题则是伴随玩家的试错及初始设计伴生，即排位赛。玩家完成新手阶段之后立即进入排位赛。但游戏的摸索成本较高，如藏品品质、面积对应的价格区间、角色、每轮过程的策略递进形态等。这些条件单独看待时，玩家都可以很容易理解，也是游戏玩法的优点之一。但也如同我们前面提及，当这些设计形成整体之后，这些元素则是以并集的形式呈现在玩家面前，形成了整体的认知负荷，对未接触过的玩家而言造成“消化不良”。
排位赛的定位偏差——“冲段位”还是“攒资产”？
《俱乐大玩家》的排位设计如下：游戏在每个场景上，分为N张地图，地图对应该次对局的主要货仓物品类型，不同场景的预估收益规模各不相同。玩家基于当下资产规模，选择不同场景进入。场景中，每个场景具有入场的上限与下限，入场的场景与玩家段位无关。这个设计的好处在于：封死玩家借助资产规模的优势，在低资产场次实现稳定规模获利，让玩家主动追逐风险。但实际上，可以采用“限制携带入场资产上限”的方式去实现，因为玩家在不同场景的藏品，原本就有收藏需求。
《俱乐大玩家》排位赛的段位设计，较大误导了玩家对玩法的权重，以为“提段位”很重要，但实际游戏机制来说是“积累资产”为首要目标。一般来说，玩家透过游戏策略最终获得排位胜利或较好排名积分，决策与胜负构成正向关联。期间，策略的正确与否透过游戏某个环节正负反馈得以印证，以此刺激玩家提升对战频次。但是，由于《俱乐大玩家》类游戏的爽感主要来自于低概率事件中 “低价拍到高净值商品”或“单局获得较高的利润收益”。整个过程中，策略与某环节的游戏反馈并非直接关联，如“A玩家的出价可以劝退其他BCD玩家出价”“B玩家透过某个决策让ACD玩家原有优势降低”等等。
相比于总资产来说，在非红藏品出现的局内，往往资产累积较为缓慢
稀有藏品的难出现，以及超价格拍卖，对于初期玩家而言的负向的心理感受强烈
另一方面在于成长意义。如同我们前文所述，德扑式估值竞拍游戏，单局游戏大部分价值商品利润由少部分商品数量构成。每一局游戏，商品的总价值存在较高的浮动属性。游戏为了不希望所有玩家成长过于增速的情况下，高稀有度商品的对局同样也会只存在少数对局。另外，“获胜”与“收益”存在分离性。这就导致：
本质类似于不同资产规模的股民进入股市进行获利，以及风险可承担规模。
中低质量对局形成的时间沉没成本高，而高质量的对局容错性低。对玩家来说，损失成本伴随的成本比一般的游戏高，除了游戏资产还有时间、心理。
“获胜”与“收益”存在较大程度分离，导致了大部分留存玩家实际上采用稳健的方式连续对局，游戏玩法自身魅力大打折扣。
爽感受限严重，因为无法知道高质量对局什么时候遇到；并且，遇到也难以透过策略提高捕获概率。
“段位”既作为实力证明，也作为一定的账号价值证明。但目前的设计来看，价值证明与实力证明都受到严重挤压，自然“段位”的意义变得可有可无。
段位的积分增减虽然有显示对应的条件，但从直观度来看依然给玩家云里雾里的感觉
信息先于策略，难度曲线“由难变易”的反常规律
作为Steam游戏的《竞拍之王》，其主要的商业模式在于角色及拍卖过程的消耗道具。虽然在Steam游戏上商业模式受到一定的诟病，但这个商业模式设计会天然亲和手游品类。用不同规模的价值针对玩家的期望值分层，依次为“小成本得大价值”>“中高成本得大价值”>“超成本得大价值”>“小成本获中价值”≥“中成本获中价值”>”中高成本获中低价值”从手游P2W的商业模式去看的话，角色、付费道具使用规模、藏品这些可以形成不同程度的付费分层。并且，不同的付费程度让游戏对局胜率、胜利获取资产规模走向不同。
本质上，德扑式估值竞拍游戏属于信息量获胜类游戏。如果将信息量与策略视为“先有鸡与先有蛋”问题的话，德扑估值类竞拍类游戏上，玩家的策略很大程度依赖于自身获取的信息度而决定，包含“真实出价时机”“真实出价范围”“真假出价幅度”等。在竞拍可选择场景与玩家持有资产规模构成硬关联下，每个玩家的容错性都是相对公平、有限的。玩家策略基于得到场上的信息规模形成决定影响，形成“先有信息，再有策略”规律，这个也会与大多数的策略类型IAP类游戏如《Ludus》《Marvel Snap》《皇室战争》《王者之弈》等“已知自己阵容，透过搭配组合形成策略”类游戏存在倒置差异。因为通常的策略型IAP类游戏上，游戏趣味性由策略体现，策略差距形成胜利数差异，胜利数决定游戏资产规模差异，达成初期的飞轮效应。玩家维持这个飞轮效应，后续由逐步增加付费、付费养成实现。
信息不等量会形成了报价差异
公有信息对所有玩家有利时，所有玩家的报价都是纯正向递增
在公有信息对玩家都不利时，诱发玩家使用道具补齐信息，形成玩家提价的底气。而提价与最终总物品价值差，构成利润
在信息劣势时，一定程度上影响报价精准度，但存在“做局”空间，让其他玩家进行高位接盘
所以在对局难度坐落规律方面，《俱乐大玩家》会基于“公有信息+私有信息+其他玩家信息+未知信息”进行博弈。玩家会基于各角色的不同，以及同角色看到的物品不同，形成估价差异，而估值道具则是进一步缩小波动范围。玩家知道信息越高，越具备报价高低的主动权。形成报价高低的二元选择；知道信息越少的玩家，在估价高低的同时，多了一层“报价真假”的二元判断。随着资产及竞拍池的提升，玩家之间的信息差落入了道具使用差异，以及防止被秒拍的报价技巧。此时，道具配合角色，在玩家处于优势环境时单场游戏的信息无限接近于透明，对局难度分布从难变易，与大多数品类游戏难度规律同样相反。要提升高资产对局的策略空间，则需要跳出仅当下该类玩法存在的游戏设计，进行内容提升式设计。如类斗地主形式的部队称+阵营化对局、对局估值竞拍转换成对高净值藏品的溢价购买、不同难度级别、机制游戏的货币转化、对抗型角色设计等等。
资产回收的三阶段机制与玩家心理博弈
资产循环方面，《俱乐大玩家》的资产回收形式是分阶段进行。
第一阶段，由玩家初期对局损失形成，尤其是透过关卡信息及玩家对其他角色、道具的不了解性，诱导玩家进行“梭哈对局”。与之配套的，则是以任务、广告位、分享、公会、战令等场景，对玩家重新补充资产。
第二阶段，则是放大角色作用及道具作用。利用角色机制与游戏场景、关卡对该角色的匹配度，形成玩家之间的差距及估值精准度差距。此时的分水岭在于：资产多的玩家会多使用道具，最终趋于“出价+道具价>单场价值”；而资产有限的玩家，错失心理逐步影响玩家的理性决策，主动风险博弈的过程形成“出价>单场价值”而回退至第一阶段。
第三阶段则是由其他游戏模式实现。在《俱乐大玩家》上后续存在休闲模式。休闲模式主要为连续5场竞拍，玩家以活动币自行购买道具及拍卖。同时，单场竞拍物的价值也会显著高于排位赛的价值。休闲模式下，玩家虽然进行连续竞拍，但一局的5场竞拍起步Token为等量，Token可被玩家自由支配于支付对局道具及出价竞拍。当5场对局之后，最后进入清算会根据玩家Token消耗的总正负收益决定排名，排名前2的玩家得到常规资产的奖金补贴。其核心目的在于，借助休闲模式培养玩家对道具使用的依赖，以及扩大玩家主动风险博弈的意愿。
所以资产循环回收上面，《俱乐大玩家》透过借助相对公平的其他游戏模式提供玩家滚动资产的形式吸引玩家主动博弈风险。但也与前文提及相同，对资产的回收及释放其实还有其他方式值得探索。
藏品馆与交易行能否撑起长期留存？
若玩家对资产得以持续的正向滚动，那么德扑式估值竞拍类游戏不可避免的存在枯燥性。所以，《俱乐大玩家》在游戏内设计藏馆系统，包含赛季收藏馆、普通的藏品收录、活动相关的系列收藏及合成等。此外，交易行也存在藏品的购买。整个游戏定调上，后续偏向以轻竞争休闲类的模拟经营游戏靠拢，包括设计的抢车位、收集藏品提升每小时资产回复等等。设计方向上，虽然合理，但较为保守。
玩法潜力巨大，但“先发制人”未必奏效
先说结论，从我们的角度来看，德扑式估值竞拍玩法的潜力实际上很高。在单一规则过程上是简化的，玩家的可操作空间并不复杂，估值伴随的猜测性也表现多样趣味。
但是，如果将这类游戏视为容易玩法移植，就大错特错。Steam游戏《竞拍之王》虽然制作成本很低，但这是因为它属于类似早年《三国杀》的规则导向类游戏，依赖于规则衍生的相关设计如每局各品质分布、深浅仓、角色与公有信息匹配区间控制、预估价格浮动程度、资产释放的正向飞轮效应与回收的负向飞轮效应等等。这类游戏在进行手游化的时候，需要考虑的是以面向受众基础开展的一系列问题：学习成本、单玩家单日体验次数、玩家成长性、爽感显著度、长期目标等。也正因如此，这个玩法进行手游化实际上需要较长的玩法周期打磨，甚至在手游化的过程中将会需要不少的定制式设计。目前涌入小游戏的《俱乐大玩家》及《全民大富豪》等游戏更多围绕“先发制人”的形式切入市场，但并不见得会比以往的其他品类游戏更易获得先发优势。
另一方面，这类玩法最大的潜力点在：它属于“所有玩家虽处于恶劣的竞争环境及关系，但在某种环境下都可以获得正向心情体验”的游戏。具体来讲，若其他玩家“做局”某一玩家，“被做局”的玩家则是负向资产形式获得拍卖品 。此时，“做局者”会认为自身技高一筹而获得快乐，但从游戏规则来讲，ta们并没有低价竞拍到商品产生利润，提升后续游戏的竞争力；同样，“被做局者”若拍卖奔着高品质藏品获得而去，即便高价拍卖也获得了自身的核心目的，虽然利润负向但满足自身核心需求。赢与输从单一的结算规则，延展至玩家实现不同目标的心理预期及反馈。
总的来看，德扑式估值竞拍这套玩法，提供了一种区别于传统竞拍、卡牌博弈的全新设计思路。它跳出了非赢即输的二元对局结果，把玩家的心理预期、收集诉求也纳入游戏反馈，博弈层面的创新值得行业参考。
但Steam端的成功，并不能简单平移到小游戏生态。高信息门槛、复杂的资产循环逻辑、爽感不可控等问题，不会依靠先发上线就自动消解。对于入局厂商而言，照搬规则只是第一步，如何做好手游化适配，下调理解门槛、优化玩家的情绪反馈，才是决定这类玩法能否跑出长线产品的关键。未来，也可以继续观察该赛道后续新品的迭代方向。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: 背包玩法进入2.0？4人韩国团队，连出两个爆款、累计收入超6000万
excerpt: 《贪婪地牢》里的装备收集和背包管理，可以在《赛菲莉娅》中找到痕迹；但这一次，团队加入了武器分支、神器联动、石板布局和多人协作，系统之间咬得更紧，构筑空间也扩大了许多。对一款动作肉鸽来说，最难得的或许也在这里：…
text:
最近一段时间，Steam上的动作肉鸽赛道又杀出了一匹黑马。
它叫《赛菲莉娅》（Sephiria）。游戏在结束约500天的抢先体验、推出1.0正式版后，同时在线峰值冲到3.4万人以上，Steam好评率稳定在94%左右。
VGI数据显示，游戏累计流水已突破580万美元，折合人民币近4000万。作为对比，它背后的开发团队TEAM HORAY，核心团队只有4人左右。
第一次打开《赛菲莉娅》，很多玩家可能不会觉得它像一款爆款。像素画面谈不上华丽，主角是一群可爱动物，故事也从“兔子村即将毁灭”这样略显传统的设定开始。
可一旦多玩几局，情况就不太对了。
你会在睡觉前惦记下一局该用什么武器，吃饭时琢磨那件神器到底该摆在哪，甚至会为了背包里的一格空间反复纠结。战斗打五分钟，整理背包十分钟，最后还觉得自己赚了。
《赛菲莉娅》真正厉害的地方，也藏在这个看起来很不起眼的背包里。
·肉鸽游戏里，第一次有人让玩家认真收拾背包
在《赛菲莉娅》中，玩家扮演兔子村的一名居民，因为提前看到了村庄被毁灭的未来，只能一次次进入高塔，寻找改变结局的方法。
每局从选择武器开始。玩家一路清理房间、挑战精英和Boss，同时收集武器升级、神器、石板与药水。死亡后，本局的大部分强化都会消失，不过可以带回部分长期资源，用来修复村庄，解锁NPC和永久天赋。
乍看之下，这套流程和常见的俯视角动作肉鸽区别不大。但《赛菲莉娅》很快就会给玩家上强度。
游戏目前有剑盾、大剑、匕首、弩、武士刀和长棍等6类武器，每一种都有自己的攻击节奏与升级路线。有人靠高频普通攻击输出，有人追求蓄力爆发，也有人围绕格挡把防御变成主要伤害来源。
武器升级数量超过200项。选中某条分支后，整局的构筑方向往往也跟着确定。比如你强化了格挡反击，后面看到提升普通攻击的装备，哪怕品质很高，也可能没有那么诱人。
接着，游戏会把神器系统摆到你面前。
正式版拥有约300件神器，它们可以提供暴击、恢复、元素异常、召唤物、法术触发等效果。一些神器单独拿出来平平无奇，凑到一起却可能形成完整的输出循环。
到这里，《赛菲莉娅》还只是一款内容量很大的动作肉鸽。真正让它长出自己模样的，是石板系统。
玩家拿到的神器需要放进网格背包，石板则会强化特定方向、直线或范围内的神器。有些位置加等级，有些位置带减益；石板本身还要占格子，背包空间却十分有限。
问题一下子多了起来：
核心神器应该放在哪？哪件道具值得吃到两块石板的加成？减益格该塞给谁？现在要不要把背包填满？万一后面掉了关键组件，又该扔掉什么？于是，每场战斗结束后的背包整理，变成了另一场战斗。
同样一批神器，随便塞进去和认真规划位置，强度可能完全不同。玩家像是在拼一张小型电路板——武器负责启动，神器负责传导，石板则决定整套机器能跑到什么功率。
TEAM HORAY曾提到，这套机制受到《Noita》法术排列系统的启发。早期版本更加复杂，团队后来把周边强化效果拆给图形更直观的石板，才逐渐形成现在的样子。
罗斯基认为，这个改动抓住了《赛菲莉娅》的命门。
在传统肉鸽里，捡到好道具通常就意味着变强；到了“赛兔”这里，掉落只是给了玩家一些零件。怎么组装和什么时候换方案，全要自己做决定。也正因为这样，玩家很难机械照抄一套攻略。
你知道某个流派很强，不代表每局都能顺利凑出来。神器掉落、石板形状、武器升级和路线奖励都会打乱计划。
前期玩家被随机性推着走，后期随着村庄功能和初始神器逐渐解锁，才开始主动追求某些构筑。等到主线通关，游戏才真正进入“研究阶段”。这种快乐很容易延续到几十甚至上百小时。
此外，《赛菲莉娅》还支持最多4人在线合作。
这款产品的场面，其实很适合直播和短视频传播。观众既能看懂一群人被Boss追着跑的狼狈，也能感受到构筑成型后满屏数字爆炸的爽感。
不过，联机也是这个小团队吃过的最大苦头之一。
接受韩国媒体Gamemeca采访时，TEAM HORAY透露，他们最初并没有按照多人游戏搭建项目。团队在开发中途决定加入联机，为此重写了大量代码，前后花费约5至6个月。此后的抢先体验阶段，断线、同步和章节进度问题也一直是更新重点。
对一个核心规模约4人的团队来说，这已经称得上一次豪赌。好在联机最终成了《赛菲莉娅》传播和长线游玩的重要支点。
·做成第二款爆款前，他们先砍掉了一个项目
TEAM HORAY是一支来自韩国龙仁的4人独立游戏团队，成立于2017年。
团队负责人安泰贤（Ahn Tae-hyun）主要负责程序开发，文智焕（Moon Ji-hwan）负责游戏策划，韩宇京（Han Woo-kyung）负责像素美术，李贤宇（Lee Hyun-woo）同样负责程序相关工作。
团队的上一款作品，是2018年发售的《贪婪地牢》（Dungreed）。这款横版动作肉鸽同样主打随机装备、像素画面和高重复游玩，并在Steam上积累了“特别好评”的口碑。
VGI估算该作流水已达到330万美元。如果再加上今年《赛菲莉娅》的流水，那么这个四人小团队的生涯总流水，已经来到了惊人的6000万人民币。
《贪婪地牢》的成功，让这群年轻开发者有了继续做独立游戏的底气。但他们没有马上复刻一款续作，而是转头开发了《Fairy Lights》。这个项目做了一段时间，甚至参加过展会，团队却始终找不到足够有力的核心玩法。
最终，他们选择停止开发。
而《赛菲莉娅》也经历过一次大改。项目最初更接近俯视角策略游戏，玩家需要指挥多个单位混战。做着做着，团队发现效果不够理想，又回到自己熟悉的动作肉鸽领域，把前作积累的战斗、随机道具和背包思路重新拆解。
《贪婪地牢》里的装备收集和背包管理，可以在《赛菲莉娅》中找到痕迹；但这一次，团队加入了武器分支、神器联动、石板布局和多人协作，系统之间咬得更紧，构筑空间也扩大了许多。
从早期构想到正式版，团队前后投入接近5年。抢先体验的约500天里，游戏经历了数十次更新。小团队做肉鸽的优势，也在这里体现出来。
·写在最后：动作肉鸽，还有很大创新空间
在罗斯基看来，《赛菲莉娅》的走红，说明动作肉鸽还有很大的创新空间。
这个品类已经挤满了作品，单纯增加武器数量和堆叠怪物，很难再让玩家记住。TEAM HORAY选择在“获得道具”之后继续追问——拿到了，然后呢？
他们给出的答案是整理与取舍。
动作战斗负责让玩家爽，随机掉落负责制造惊喜，背包和石板则让每次掉落都变成一道题。到了高难度和多人模式，这道题还会不断出现新的解法。
很多游戏用几小时展示完所有新鲜感，《赛菲莉娅》却要等玩家逐渐理解系统后，才开始露出最有意思的部分。
对一款动作肉鸽来说，最难得的或许也在这里：玩到第100个小时，捡起一件熟悉的神器，玩家依然可能停在原地，然后心甘情愿地打开背包再算一遍。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: D&D is getting a Netflix series about Strahd, involving the director of The Prisoner of Azkaban, and I honestly think this could work great
author: Harvey Randall
text:
Curse of Strahd is one of the most popular D&D modules for a reason—it's actually really compelling. Set in the misty, cursed lands of Barovia, Curse of Strahd is dominated by the titular Strahd von Zarovich, a vampire lord with a tragic backstory and a propensity for showing up at random intervals to give you a fantasy wedgie.
In the one Strahd campaign I played in, my first encounter with the man involved him bleeding our cleric and making my thief drink his blood—so, you know. Normal.
Anyway, per Deadline , we'll be getting a fully-fledged live action Netflix series about him dubbed Ravenloft—after the wider set of domains that darklords like Mr. Zarovich himself enjoy dominion over. It's being helmed by writer and executive producer John August and executive producer Alfonso Cuarón.
The latter of which worked on Harry Potter: The Prisoner of Azkaban. Fittingly, one of the darker Harry Potter films—and owner of exactly the kind of murky, grey aesthetic I'd anticipate in any series taking place in Ravenloft.
The report reads: "Described as a prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance, Ravenloft and its Domains of Dread tackle adventure through character-driven stories of dark magic and supernatural intrigue.
"At its heart, the series follows the making of the vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovich, whose story of power, love, obsession, and undead transformation charts his origins from tragic antihero to one of Dungeons & Dragons’ most notorious villains."
And hey, genuinely? I think this could work out great, assuming it can escape the executive Netflix meddling and second-screen scriptwriting that's been creeping its wormy fingers into games recently. Strahd's entire backstory is tragic enough and appealing enough that unwinding it underpins one of the most popular D&D modules.
I look forward to the season finale where, presumably, a group of four adventurers with increasingly absurd backstories and a sword made out of sunlight punt down his front door and kick his byronic ass.

title: A popular streamer turned down a 6-figure deal to play Arc Raiders because 'the game frustrated me so much'
author: Elie Gould
text:
Everyone has a price. Maybe it's $100, maybe it's $1,000, maybe it's for someone to see your innate value as a human being, or maybe it's $1,000,000. Popular streamer TimTheTatman recently revealed what it would take to get him to go back to Arc Raiders , and spoilers, it's not the third option.
There was apparently an ad deal floating around for the Arc Raiders and Subway collab, which TimTheTatman was approached for, but did not entertain. "I did say no to six-figures with Arc Raiders, I did," he revealed in a stream earlier this week. "I said 'No thank you'. And it was the Subway Arc Raiders ad. I said I just can't do it, I'm sorry."
(Image credit: Embark) This was met with the exact response you'd expect with people being baffled that he'd ever think of turning down such a lucrative offer. "That's kind of the funny part of being in a streamer position," TimTheTatman continued. "People say 'you're a fucking sellout' but then in the same breath I said I passed on six-figures from Arc Raiders and people are like 'you're fucking stupid'."
He revealed that he does actually have a price to play Arc Raiders again: they'd just have had to add another zero onto the offer. "If that Arc Raiders deal was seven-figures—hey boys welcome back to Arc Raiders and Subway, right, you see what I'm saying? 100% we're going back. But it's just for me, the game frustrated me so much—I got frustrated so much with that game, I just don't want to play it ever again. Even to a point where six-figures isn't going to get me back on it."
I can't say I'm surprised. Arc Raiders is in a bit of a rough spot right now, especially for streamers, what with all the cheating and stream sniping. Embark Studios' executive producer Aleksander Grøndal recently admitted the shortcomings of Arc Raiders and promised that its upcoming major update Frozen Trails will reset the game and provide enough incentive to get players to come back, though—even if they don't get a six-figure deal to do it.

title: I have filled GTA 5 with realistic Los Angeles snow
author: Joshua Wolens
text:
Los Santos Customs
I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .
Okay, two things. First: Los Santos Customs will be taking a hiatus next week, as I spend nine days in a row sleeping and attempting to develop the antibodies to counter whatever exotic German illness it is I acquired at Gamescom 2026 .
Second: it's snowing in Los Santos, just like the real-life LA.
(Image credit: Rockstar) I have installed WinterV Beta , with the aim of making Grand Theft Auto 5's weather a little more interesting than it usually is. The pitch is simple: what if there was snow? Well, reader, having played a little GTA 5 with WinterV Beta, I can assure you that there very much is snow. Plus, all the world's lighting takes on a kind of a sickly, ochre hue, which is also just like LA.
From the sky: flurries of flakes. On the roads: cars covered in a sheen of powder, tyre-chains inexplicably equipped (the snow does not, in my version of GTA 5 where a significant chunk of the exterior map has absconded to the phantom zone, settle). In the air: a crisp winter chill. Santa Claus is coming to town; fire a truck at him .
I can't tell you if the presence of snow on the city roads impacts car handling because, as we have established, cars in my GTA 5 no longer have handling . Nevertheless, it does change the vibe quite a lot. As someone who's spent a lot of the last month looking at GTA 5—a change is as good as a rest.
But also, it is time for a rest. I will see you the week after next, whereupon we'll probably finally convert this game into GTA 6. I can feel it.

title: The Blood of Dawnwalker endings and how to get each one
author: Sean Martin
text:
It took me quite a while to work out all The Blood of Dawnwalker endings . Similar to The Witcher 3, there are a fair few different options, each with a number of variables that can change based on your choices. There are also some secret endings to discover.
Obviously, this guide will contain spoilers for just about everything, you've been warned. Here's each ending, how they work, plus a short explainer about the epilogue and its different outcomes.
All Blood of Dawnwalker endings
There are seven possible endings to Blood of Dawnwalker.
Four involve assaulting Griefberg Castle, either with allies, or by yourself.
One involves making a deal with Brencis.
The final two endings are secret and accomplished before the others.
Also two additional notes:
The post-credit cutscene plays in every ending.
Lunka's fate is the same in every ending.
All endings, except for one of the secret ones, involve an epilogue sequence which runs through decisions you made throughout the game—and there are some big differences, but I'll explain all of those in the epilogue section at the end if you're curious. Side note, make sure to have 800 Denarius on hand for any ending involving the epilogue , as the church will ask for a donation and you can give your sister Yanna a dowry.
Assaulting Griefberg Castle
You'll fight the Vrakhiri boyars in the castle if you don't defeat them before Rebel Wolves If you run out of time, you can still assault the castle, but it's too late for your family Rebel Wolves Four of the game's endings begin with assaulting Griefberg Castle, and in every version, your assault changes based on a few key variables:
If Ambrus or Bakir are still alive you'll have to fight them as bosses during the castle assault, with Ambrus in the entrance hall and Bakir in the dungeon. Bakir will also force you to fight some of the prisoners if he's present.
If you killed Xanthe , you won't face her as a boss in the throneroom, but you'll have to complete her trap sequence , which involves additional combat and puzzling.
If your 30 day timer has run out , your family is dead, but you will have realised that by the cutscene that plays when you run out of time. After this point, you can keep playing the game without a timer, but the absence of your family impacts aspects of the epilogue.
Below, I'll run through each variation of the castle assault.
A Lone Wolf's Hunt
You can either Shadow Step over the castle walls or go in via the side door if you've secured Father Florin's support (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) Coen takes the fight to Brencis by himself.
Unlock conditions
Shadow Step over the wall of Griefberg Castle at nighttime.
Or find Father Florin's hideout in Svartrau cathedral, track him down, and complete A Hero's End, which unlocks the ability to enter the castle in the day using a password at a sidedoor.
This ending sees Coen assault Griefberg Castle by himself at either day or night, depending on which of the approaches you take. If you do fight Ambrus, Bakir, or Xanthe in the assault, you won't be able to drink their Vrakhir blood and gain their abilities if it's daytime, or invite them in, and will instead just kill them.
First off, you always have to fight the Unblinking Blasphemy boss, even if you completed the Who Pulls the Strings quest for the Manumits. You battle through the castle, free some prisoners by unlocking their cells, and eventually confront Brencis in the dungeon depths, just in time to save your family.
You can either fight Brencis here, or make a deal with him if you agree to bow and give up either Crake and the Manumits, or Lacra, though if it's the former, you'll have to go their hideout and mark it, as in the A Deal With the Devil ending (I'll explain that one in its dedicated section below).
If you assault the castle by night, you'll have to fight every battle in vampire form (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) If not, you'll fight and defeat Brencis, and choose whether to invite him in, or leave him in Anachora (vampire hell) to have his soul devoured. After this, the epilogue sequence in Laslea will begin.
This is genuinely one of my favorite endings—Vale Sangora becomes independent and there's some degree of lawlessness, but the Manumits protect the valley from the worst enterprising ruffians. You can read a proclamation on a tree in Laslea explaining that Svartrau city council plans to petition Bohemia, Hungary, or Poland to join their realms in the spring.
Since there are no more Vrakhiri, the plague returns, the Uriashi return to their villages, but Christianity also returns, the cathedral is restored, and Father Florin becomes a saint. I'm sure you're thinking " That's a good ending??" but just wait until I explain the others.
Rise At Dawn, Fall Before Dusk
This ending follows Marat and the Manumits (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) Coen helps Crake and the Manumits restore Catalin Dragosti to power.
Unlock conditions
Join the Manumits via The Firebrand, Shadows in the Woods, and Where Loyalty Lies , and then follow the questline until you complete Who Pulls the Strings.
In this ending, Crake explains that Catalin Dragosti (the son of Vale Sangora's former tyrant) is waiting outside the valley with an army, and you attack Eastridge Outpost to let him in.
Unsurprisingly, Catalin Dragosti is as bloodthirsty as his father and immediately executes some defenceless prisoners, though you can save at least two of them if you object. After Rise at Dawn, you attack Griefberg Castle in Fall Before Dusk, infiltrating through the tunnels below and battling some Kobolds.
The key variations here are that you won't save any of the prisoners, since Brencis knew you were coming. Vlad will also get a load of Manumits killed by rushing the gate if you save him in the intro , and encourage his recklessness in the Old Friends, New Friends quest where you talk to him in the Manumit hideout.
Finally, you'll reach the throne room, where Brencis will try to murder Catalin Dragosti.
If you let Brencis try to kill Catalin , Crake will rush forward instead and die defending him.
If you save Catalin , both he and Crake will live.
After this, you'll continue to the banquet hall, with or without Crake, and will fight Brencis in a room with your family tied to chairs. Unlike the A Lone Wolf's Hunt ending, you can't make a deal with Brencis at this point, since you can't stop Catalin and his army. You'll fight and defeat Brencis, invite him in, or leave him in hell, and the epilogue in Laslea will play.
You'll assault Eastridge outpost so Catalin Dragosti's army can enter the valley Rebel Wolves If you choose to not save Catalin in the throne room, Marat will die instead Rebel Wolves This is one of the worst endings in my opinion. Catalin Dragosti undertakes a campaign of retribution against anyone he sees as having helped the Vrakhiri, burning entire districts of Svartrau and filling the castle dungeons. As you see in a note on a tree in Laslea, he also imposes a large tax and encourages people to inform on each other. The epilogue also mentions his mercenary army loots and pillages towns whenever it feels like it.
Perhaps the most heartbreaking part of this ending is it reveals who Crake really is—a toady for Catalin. Under Dragosti's orders, he undertakes a genocide of the Uriashi, seeing them as monsters just like the Vrakhiri. The plague also returns, as does Christianity, but there is a slight silver lining in that this is the only epilogue where you can talk to Crake in Laslea.
Midnight Reckoning
This ending involves allying with Lacra to take down Brencis (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) Coen helps Lacra end Brencis' sinister scheme.
Unlock conditions
Meet Lacra during the A Friend Like This quest, which you most likely get via the note on Ambrus's body in The Gilded Gauntlet , and then follow her questline until you unlock Midnight Reckoning.
Alongside Lacra, you enter the Griefberg Castle dungeons via the ancient ruins below and destroy Brencis's ritual, before ascending through the castle to face Brencis himself. The key variables here are that in smashing the ritual, Lacra unleashes hell on the castle. Corpses start coming back to life, huge chunks of the castle are ripped up into the air, and the prisoners lose their minds.
When you finally reach the throne room, your family will be overgrown in the red roots (but still alive). Brencis will appear to confront you and Lacra.
If you betray Lacra and choose your family , she'll fight Brencis, but he'll win and drink her blood. The outcome here is the same as the A Deal With The Devil ending (explained below).
If you fight Brencis with Lacra , you can still save your family. I haven't played this variant to confirm, but there's a cutscene midfight that implies Lacra dies if you didn't complete her optional The Night of Horrors quest and eat the Mandrake with her.
As with the other endings, you'll defeat Brencis in Anachora, and can decide whether to invite him in, or let him be consumed by hell. It took me quite a while to work out all The Blood of Dawnwalker endings. Similar to The Witcher 3, there are a fair few different options, each with a number of variables that can change based on your choices. There are also some secret endings to discover.

Obviously, this guide will contain spoilers for just about everything, you've been warned. Here's each ending, how they work, plus a short explainer about the epilogue and its different outcomes.

All Blood of Dawnwalker endings

There are seven possible endings to Blood of Dawnwalker.

  • Four involve assaulting Griefberg Castle, either with allies, or by yourself.
  • One involves making a deal with Brencis.
  • The final two endings are secret and accomplished before the others.

Also two additional notes:

  • The post-credit cutscene plays in every ending.
  • Lunka's fate is the same in every ending.

All endings, except for one of the secret ones, involve an epilogue sequence which runs through decisions you made throughout the game—and there are some big differences, but I'll explain all of those in the epilogue section at the end if you're curious. Side note, make sure to have 800 Denarius on hand for any ending involving the epilogue, as the church will ask for a donation and you can give your sister Yanna a dowry.

Assaulting Griefberg Castle

Four of the game's endings begin with assaulting Griefberg Castle, and in every version, your assault changes based on a few key variables:

  • If Ambrus or Bakir are still alive you'll have to fight them as bosses during the castle assault, with Ambrus in the entrance hall and Bakir in the dungeon. Bakir will also force you to fight some of the prisoners if he's present.
  • If you killed Xanthe, you won't face her as a boss in the throneroom, but you'll have to complete her trap sequence, which involves additional combat and puzzling.
  • If your 30 day timer has run out, your family is dead, but you will have realised that by the cutscene that plays when you run out of time. After this point, you can keep playing the game without a timer, but the absence of your family impacts aspects of the epilogue.

Below, I'll run through each variation of the castle assault.

A Lone Wolf's Hunt

Coen takes the fight to Brencis by himself.

Unlock conditions

  • Shadow Step over the wall of Griefberg Castle at nighttime.
  • Or find Father Florin's hideout in Svartrau cathedral, track him down, and complete A Hero's End, which unlocks the ability to enter the castle in the day using a password at a sidedoor.

This ending sees Coen assault Griefberg Castle by himself at either day or night, depending on which of the approaches you take. If you do fight Ambrus, Bakir, or Xanthe in the assault, you won't be able to drink their Vrakhir blood and gain their abilities if it's daytime, or invite them in, and will instead just kill them.

First off, you always have to fight the Unblinking Blasphemy boss, even if you completed the Who Pulls the Strings quest for the Manumits. You battle through the castle, free some prisoners by unlocking their cells, and eventually confront Brencis in the dungeon depths, just in time to save your family.

You can either fight Brencis here, or make a deal with him if you agree to bow and give up either Crake and the Manumits, or Lacra, though if it's the former, you'll have to go their hideout and mark it, as in the A Deal With the Devil ending (I'll explain that one in its dedicated section below).

If not, you'll fight and defeat Brencis, and choose whether to invite him in, or leave him in Anachora (vampire hell) to have his soul devoured. After this, the epilogue sequence in Laslea will begin.

This is genuinely one of my favorite endings—Vale Sangora becomes independent and there's some degree of lawlessness, but the Manumits protect the valley from the worst enterprising ruffians. You can read a proclamation on a tree in Laslea explaining that Svartrau city council plans to petition Bohemia, Hungary, or Poland to join their realms in the spring.

Since there are no more Vrakhiri, the plague returns, the Uriashi return to their villages, but Christianity also returns, the cathedral is restored, and Father Florin becomes a saint. I'm sure you're thinking "That's a good ending??" but just wait until I explain the others.

Rise At Dawn, Fall Before Dusk

Coen helps Crake and the Manumits restore Catalin Dragosti to power.

Unlock conditions

  • Join the Manumits via The Firebrand, Shadows in the Woods, and Where Loyalty Lies, and then follow the questline until you complete Who Pulls the Strings.

In this ending, Crake explains that Catalin Dragosti (the son of Vale Sangora's former tyrant) is waiting outside the valley with an army, and you attack Eastridge Outpost to let him in.

Unsurprisingly, Catalin Dragosti is as bloodthirsty as his father and immediately executes some defenceless prisoners, though you can save at least two of them if you object. After Rise at Dawn, you attack Griefberg Castle in Fall Before Dusk, infiltrating through the tunnels below and battling some Kobolds.

The key variations here are that you won't save any of the prisoners, since Brencis knew you were coming. Vlad will also get a load of Manumits killed by rushing the gate if you save him in the intro, and encourage his recklessness in the Old Friends, New Friends quest where you talk to him in the Manumit hideout.

Finally, you'll reach the throne room, where Brencis will try to murder Catalin Dragosti.

  • If you let Brencis try to kill Catalin, Crake will rush forward instead and die defending him.
  • If you save Catalin, both he and Crake will live.

After this, you'll continue to the banquet hall, with or without Crake, and will fight Brencis in a room with your family tied to chairs. Unlike the A Lone Wolf's Hunt ending, you can't make a deal with Brencis at this point, since you can't stop Catalin and his army. You'll fight and defeat Brencis, invite him in, or leave him in hell, and the epilogue in Laslea will play.

This is one of the worst endings in my opinion. Catalin Dragosti undertakes a campaign of retribution against anyone he sees as having helped the Vrakhiri, burning entire districts of Svartrau and filling the castle dungeons. As you see in a note on a tree in Laslea, he also imposes a large tax and encourages people to inform on each other. The epilogue also mentions his mercenary army loots and pillages towns whenever it feels like it.

Perhaps the most heartbreaking part of this ending is it reveals who Crake really is—a toady for Catalin. Under Dragosti's orders, he undertakes a genocide of the Uriashi, seeing them as monsters just like the Vrakhiri. The plague also returns, as does Christianity, but there is a slight silver lining in that this is the only epilogue where you can talk to Crake in Laslea.

Midnight Reckoning

Coen helps Lacra end Brencis' sinister scheme.

Unlock conditions

  • Meet Lacra during the A Friend Like This quest, which you most likely get via the note on Ambrus's body in The Gilded Gauntlet, and then follow her questline until you unlock Midnight Reckoning.

Alongside Lacra, you enter the Griefberg Castle dungeons via the ancient ruins below and destroy Brencis's ritual, before ascending through the castle to face Brencis himself. The key variables here are that in smashing the ritual, Lacra unleashes hell on the castle. Corpses start coming back to life, huge chunks of the castle are ripped up into the air, and the prisoners lose their minds.

When you finally reach the throne room, your family will be overgrown in the red roots (but still alive). Brencis will appear to confront you and Lacra.

  • If you betray Lacra and choose your family, she'll fight Brencis, but he'll win and drink her blood. The outcome here is the same as the A Deal With The Devil ending (explained below).
  • If you fight Brencis with Lacra, you can still save your family. I haven't played this variant to confirm, but there's a cutscene midfight that implies Lacra dies if you didn't complete her optional The Night of Horrors quest and eat the Mandrake with her.

As with the other endings, you'll defeat Brencis in Anachora, and can decide whether to invite him in, or let him be consumed by hell. However, he'll also reveal more in this ending about his plan—that he wanted to accept and harness the curse of Anachora that all vampires harbor instead of trying to resist it.

This ending isn't a particularly good one—as with A Lone Wolf's Hunt, Vale Sangora becomes independent for a time, the Manumits defend it, and both Christianity and the plague return. The negative here is basically everyone in the castle dies and it remains a cursed hellscape.

Lacra also doesn't trust you enough to tell you that this was going to happen and could've killed your family, which is a sad realisation about her character and goals. Lacra will appear briefly in the epilogue, but she appears in almost every epilogue provided you complete her questline. Taking this route to the ending also doesn't change her ending in the epilogue.

A Deal With The Devil

Coen makes a deal with Brencis for the freedom of Laslea.

Unlock conditions

  • Reach max level infamy (by killing Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe).

In this ending, you meet Brencis at Shrike's Crag, the haunted site of a mass atrocity committed by Skender Dragosti (the valley's former tyrant). After meeting your father, who Brencis brings, he'll offer you a deal: He'll return your family and the villagers, and you can live in Laslea, exempt from the blood tax, if you find and mark the Manumit hideout.

You can also choose to kill Brencis here, though spilling any blood summons the dead, and you'll have to fight him with a million ghosts trying to get in the way. This is also inadvisable because you leave your father, Pieter, to the mercy of all the angry spirits you summon, which will lead to his death. Before you can agree to Brencis's deal, your father picks the absolute worst moment to trip over and hurt himself, summoning a legion of ghosts you have to fight through with Brencis to escape and save him.

All you have to do to complete this ending is head to the Manumit hideout and mark the door. Brencis swoops in, murders the Manumits, drags Crake out into the street, drinks his blood, and then disappears with him—not a great outcome for Crake, obviously. However, the epilogue in Laslea will play out.

This ending is not great. While it's made clear that Brencis's regime does eventually fall thanks to the Arbiters, bad stuff happens to Lacra and Father Florin, and Brencis continues to rule with an iron fist, slowly bleeding the valley for his scheme. The upsides are that the plague doesn't return, the Uriashi stick around, and Laslea gets to practice Christianity as an exception.

Secret endings

Leaving Vale Sangora

Coen leaves the valley to its fate and hits the bricks.

Unlock conditions

  • Reach Corruption Level 11 and unlock the second level of Shadow Dweller in the vampirism tree.

This is probably my favorite ending for Blood of Dawnwalker. You can do it anytime after the prologue provided you reach Level 11 Corruption and unlock the second level of Shadow Dweller in the vampirism skill tree, increasing the max distance of Shadow Step. Head to the Cursed Chasm in northwest Briar Sloughs, following the road that looks like it leads out of Vale Sangora.

Use the max level Shadow Step to get across the gap and follow the road to the still open pass. You'll be given the choice to leave the valley forever or stay. That's it. There isn't even an epilogue (besides the post-credit cutscene), so it really is a disavowal of everything in Vale Sangora, as Coen leaves with his newfound vampirism to make a new life.

Killing Brencis in the prologue

Coen thwarts Brencis's scheme without leaving Laslea.

Unlock conditions:

  • Defeat Brencis when you fight him at the end of the prologue and then defeat Brencis, Grotesque Ascendent.

As many of you likely guessed, saw, or experienced yourself, if you manage to beat Brencis's first stage in the prologue, you can defeat him there and end the game. I'm going to be frank—it's not worth it. Defeating both the Brencis fights in the prologue is incredibly hard, even on the lowest difficulty, and the ending isn't that much different from A Lone Wolf's Hunt.

The main difference is that the epilogue is, understandably, short as hell because you didn't do anything in the game.

The Blood of Dawnwalker's epilogue explained

The epilogue in Laslea has a few different variables depending on the ending you chose:

  • Certain characters showing up in the town.
  • The characters who appear in the scene with Lunka at the end are different.
  • The notices on the tree in the town square can change, but invariably address who rules Vale Sangora, whether Christianity returned, whether you killed the Murohn in Svartrau Cathedral's Almshouse, and the fate of St. Tyna's Convent.

Below I'll run through the epilogue section post-Laslea, which shows you a series of tableaus you can examine. These explain the outcomes of various quests and choices you made:

Your family

  • Your mother will be absent if you didn't make Anca's medicine correctly and she was killed in the prologue.
  • Your family will be dead and absent if you don't save them in 30 days.
  • Lunka will be corrupted by Brencis—her and Coen always leave the valley at the end after meeting Neberu.

Svartrau, The Plague, and the Uriashi

  • The Uriashi will either retreat to the mountain or stay.

title: Me: You can now run DLSS 5 on AMD GPUs. My RX 9070 XT: Please stop, it hurts us
author: Dave James
text:
Another day, another DLSS 5 story that actually kinda doesn't involve Nvidia itself doing anything, because it seems now AMD GPU owners can get in on the act. A new homebrew app has been released on Github that will allow you to run the DLSS Neural Rendering feature on a Radeon GPU. I've tried it and it works, but damn does it hurt the poor Radeon silicon.
From having DLSS 5 .dll files plucked from an early access version of NBA 2K27, we've had modders working hard to create surprisingly polished ways to essentially get the tech working in practically any game , even if it doesn't natively support traditional DLSS itself.
I've been playing around with it a lot this past week, even to the point of jamming it into Football Manager 26 just to see what would happen. And, y'know what, I kinda like the result so I'm keeping it. I wasn't expecting that, and I also wasn't expecting this technology, created by Nvidia, to appear so quickly on AMD GPUs. Historically we've found that where Nvidia goes, so AMD follows, at least in the GPU feature space, but it seems like AMD might not actually have to do much this time. Well, apart from actually make the silicon a little more tensor-friendly.
Because I have spent the afternoon trying to get the new app from user danielblnc on Github to work on my Radeon RX 9070 XT in Cyberpunk 2077. Essentially you download the DLSS-NR-on-AMD file, drop it into the relevant folder (the bin/x64 folder in the Cyberpunk 2077 directory in Steam, for example) and run it. So long as you have the necessary nvngx_dlssnr.dll file that's been doing the rounds installed in the same place it ought to work.
It didn't.
Initially Windows flagged it as containing a virus, but I did some checking around with VirusTotal and seemingly the Defender flag is a machine learning false positive. Probably. But even then I still struggled to have it running happily.
I am not entirely sure what I did wrong, but when I enabled the feature in-game all I got was a black output where the 3D world ought to be, even though the HUD and game kept on running. After some file deletion, redownloading, verifying of integrity (mine and Cyberpunk's), and a rollback of my AMD Adrenalin drivers, I finally got it working. Kinda. I mean it's still kinda crashy, and I can only now launch Cyberpunk 2077 directly from the .exe file rather than from Steam, but it works.
But my poor GPU wished I hadn't. Now, we know that DLSS 5 is a hell of a resource hog on an RTX 50-series GPU that it's designed for, with a touted 50 - 60% performance hit officially noted by Nvidia , so I should have known it would trouble the AMD GPU.
DLSS NR on Nvidia
DLSS 5 was designed for GeForce GPUs, so is a little more capable, but still a massive resource hog.
DLSS NR Off
DLSS NR On
Still… running at 4K RT Ultra settings is tough enough, and I was getting just 61 fps on the RX 9070 XT even with FSR 4 set to Balanced. And then flicking the DLSS Neural Rendering toggle to 'on' made that figure drop to just 9 fps.
And I thought the 73% drop Andy found with NBA 2K27 was rough.
DLSS NR on AMD
AMD GPUs running DLSS 5 looks great, but runs horribly.
DLSS NR Off
DLSS NR On
Now it's worth noting that the fact it is running at all on AMD GPUs is impressive on its own, but it's not going to make any Radeon graphics card owners any happier about it when they're getting unplayable frame rates out of their new ill-gotten pretties. An 85% performance drop is not sustainable. Nice for screenshots though, eh?
The issue is that AMD's RDNA 4 doesn't have the level of dedicated silicon for the sort of matrix calculations the feature is running… in the same way that RTX 20-series chips don't.
(Image credit: CDPR) The Turing architecture does have Tensor Cores, but they're far weaker compared to those in the RTX 40- or RTX 50-series, and the shared resources AMD plucks from the standard RDNA 4 Compute Units for these sorts of calculations aren't as robust either. Hence the weaker performance.
Will they be able to squeeze more performance out of this feature on AMD chips? I don't know, but YouTuber Ancient Gameplays noted the app in a recent video, and states that performance has gone up 12% since the first version of the DLSS-NR-on-AMD software first hit Github, so maybe there's a chance. But, realistically, I think there's a hard hardware limit in there which is going to stop DLSS Neural Rendering from being a realistic part of AMD's armoury in this generation.

DLSS NR Off
DLSS NR On

Still… running at 4K RT Ultra settings is tough enough, and I was getting just 61 fps on the RX 9070 XT even with FSR 4 set to Balanced. And then flicking the DLSS Neural Rendering toggle to 'on' made that figure drop to just 9 fps.

And I thought the 73% drop Andy found with NBA 2K27 was rough.

DLSS NR on AMD

AMD GPUs running DLSS 5 looks great, but runs horribly.

DLSS NR Off
DLSS NR On

Now it's worth noting that the fact it is running at all on AMD GPUs is impressive on its own, but it's not going to make any Radeon graphics card owners any happier about it when they're getting unplayable frame rates out of their new ill-gotten pretties. An 85% performance drop is not sustainable. Nice for screenshots though, eh?

The issue is that AMD's RDNA 4 doesn't have the level of dedicated silicon for the sort of matrix calculations the feature is running… in the same way that RTX 20-series chips don't.

The Turing architecture does have Tensor Cores, but they're far weaker compared to those in the RTX 40- or RTX 50-series, and the shared resources AMD plucks from the standard RDNA 4 Compute Units for these sorts of calculations aren't as robust either. Hence the weaker performance.

Will they be able to squeeze more performance out of this feature on AMD chips? I don't know, but YouTuber Ancient Gameplays noted the app in a recent video, and states that performance has gone up 12% since the first version of the DLSS-NR-on-AMD software first hit Github, so maybe there's a chance. But, realistically, I think there's a hard hardware limit in there which is going to stop DLSS Neural Rendering from being a realistic part of AMD's armoury in this generation.

title: The White House launches online 'arcade' with its own takes on Tetris and other popular games, and it's as rotten as you'd expect
author: Andy Chalk
text:
The White House, the epicenter of power in the most powerful nation in human history, has rolled out a new online arcade on its website. And yes, it is every bit as racist, repugnant, and creatively bankrupt as you'd expect.
We'll set aside the question of "why?" for now and get straight to the games, beginning with Flappy Bill, a game in which you fly a bald eagle down the National Mall. It's not clear whether the bird's name is actually Bill because it's also carrying a bill, which my young years of being exposed to Schoolhouse Rock from across the border taught me is part of the US lawmaking process, or at least used to be before they decided that having the president do everything by fiat is more efficient or something. In any event, it's an entirely unremarkable Flappy Bird clone, innocuous but about as much fun as tying a shoelace.
The tone takes a hard turn to the right with the next game, Build the Wall: Zombie Border Siege, a Tetris knock-off where you'll "protect the border from the coming horde." To ensure there's no misunderstanding the nature of this horde, the game's backdrop is a retro-future take on the sun setting over a barren desert—and in case that's too subtle, there's also a sign that says "Southern Border."
One notable thing about this one is that unlike actual Tetris, the lines don't disappear when they're completed. Instead, they just stack up until they reach the top, at which point it's inevitably game over no matter how neatly you've arranged things. A slow-moving line of "zombies" moves across the bottom of the screen, and they are capable of getting past your wall if you haven't built it high enough—but "high enough" is literally two stacked tetrominoes, after which nothing can get past. So I'm not sure what the point is there, except to be really racist and xenophobic, I suppose.
(Image credit: White House) Moving on: The third game in the White House Arcade is called Rio Run, a recreation of a "border patrol along the Rio Grande" based on the ancient classic Snake. As a balding white guy in a suit, you pick up brown-skinned people one at a time, each of whom joins a train behind you wearing shackles and an orange jumpsuit. Once the game ends, when you run into a wall or your train of prisoners, they're all deported and you're encouraged to try again. Lovely.
I don't really know what to make of the fourth game. Supply Line, as it's called, charges you to "sort the school line to make America healthy again" by letting 'good' food ride a conveyor belt to the school lunch box, while chucking 'bad' food—anything with coloring, additives, sealed packages, or seed oils—into the "reject" box.
This one was a little tricky at first because the low-effort graphics make it difficult to tell good food from bad (as the concept is envisioned by Robert F. Kennedy Jr), but what's really bizarre is the muscular Black man in boxing gloves standing in the background. Every time I let a bad bit of food slip past, he punched the back of my monitor. Four punches and it was game over, although oddly enough he's the one who took the actual damage.
Also, reading labels is apparently bad, according to a sign with a red strike through it. Ain't that America? For you and me, baby.
In my country we encourage reading the labels. (Image credit: White House) The fifth and final game on the White Hours Arcade tour is Trump Savings Tycoon, a game about filling your kids' Trump Accounts , which are basically retirement savings accounts for children, backed by money from various super-wealthy individuals like Jensen Huang and Michael Dell who may or may not have anything to gain from big-money sycophancy.
This game involves simply clicking on various money-esque objects with a net as they fly across the sky. It's maybe the simplest of the bunch mechanically, but the clicking is extremely imprecise so it doesn't take long before three objects are missed and it's game over.
More interesting to me is the background, which features the Reflecting Pool (a perfectly lovely shade of blue, unlike its real-world counterpart ) and a massive construction crane looming over the Washington DC skyline, presumably indicating optimism about the president's planned ballroom/bunker. There's also a small convoy of what appears to be flying police cars that goes soaring across the sky every now and then. I have no theories about what that might be about.
In case it wasn't sufficiently clear, these things are universally bad, both conceptually and in execution: If you're going to rip off the world's most famous stacking game to promote your racist agenda, for instance, you should at least make it play like that game. It's an astonishingly lazy effort, and I can't shake the feeling that all of these games were vibe-coded, maybe by some DOGE hanger-on they found hiding in the bathroom.
The obvious question is, as noted earlier, is why? Who are these games for? I think the answer in one sense is that they're for no one in particular, but are instead just another wave in the flood of sewage pumped out every day by the US president and his administration. Over the last couple years, the US government has posted numerous gaming-related memes , video clips , and AI generated images to promote its leader and his agenda.
But more broadly, this effort is targeted at the young male gamer demographic, at least in part to leverage the political influence it first demonstrated during the Gamergate harassment campaign.
George E. Osborn, author of Power Play: Videogames, Politics, and the Battle for Global Influence , wrote on his Videogames Industry Memo blog (via The Guardian ) that "the content works because it does what a lot of good social content does. It riffs on widely known popular culture to get cut through in the way many popular memes do. It has a chaotic, anarchic tone which suits the channel it's in. It is transgressive in a way that delights the administration's supporters and infuriates its rivals. And it feels all the more edgy because the formerly stuffy White House social channels have been turned into a place where this kind of stuff circulates freely.
"A big chunk of the modern political right in America emerged from Gamergate. The hate movement was brought into the political fold by Steve Bannon and Breitbart after it showed how it is possible to wash extreme talking points into the mainstream political environment. Its members became online 'shock troopers' for Trump, as well as becoming foundational figures in the alt-right and nuttier fringes like QAnon. And as they've grown up, the almost entirely young men who made waves back in 2014 are now in positions of power on the right. This allows them to shape the online narrative, encouraging them to reach a fresh generation of men through an increasingly fragmented social media ecosystem that allows transgressive macho 'manosphere' content to trend."
The US government shows no sign of easing off on these behaviors. Posts on X promoting the new arcade site include animations using the Xbox, Nintendo, and Sega logos, the latter of which was probably chosen because it morphs well into "MAGA."
CAN'T STOP WINNING. 🎮Build the wall. Deport. Fill a Trump Account. LIVE - PLAY NOW 📲 https://t.co/qIR69AxSnm pic.twitter.com/2nr2jG1ZRg September 3, 2026
While the owners of properties used in past posts have thus far opted to stay silent, The Tetris Company did obliquely suggest that it might take a more aggressive approach. Following an Instagram post in which the company said "we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," it added, "PS: The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of Build the Wall. PPS: We take copyright infringement very seriously."
A post shared by Tetris (@tetris_official)
A photo posted by
As completely crappy as all of this is on every possible level, it seems likely there's more to come. A currently unoccupied sixth game window on the White House Arcade page says "a new adventure awaits," and encourages interested followers to "stay tuned." I've reached out to the White House for comment on the new virtual arcade and will update if I receive a reply.

title: After a massive 2021 office expansion, Bungie is now trying to sublease its 211,000 square foot headquarters
author: Lincoln Carpenter
text:
In 2021, as studio CEO Pete Parsons cited the company's recent "tremendous growth and opportunity," Bungie announced its plans for a massive expansion to its Bellevue, Washington headquarters . The campus embiggening, which internal sources have reportedly described as costing "hundreds of millions" of dollars, more than doubled the size of Bungie's offices from 84,000 square feet to just under 211,000.
Now, after five and a half years of spending sprees, publisher acquisitions, stumbling product launches, project cancellations, and repeated mass layoffs, Bungie appears to be seeking subletters for the goliath game development headquarters it's no longer capable of filling.
According to a 10-page leasing brochure reviewed by The Game Post , Bungie is seeking interested renters to sublease its expansive headquarters, listing its 210,984 square feet as a "turn-key" production facility. In addition to expected office fixtures, the listing also features a dedicated lobby, gym and exercise facilities (including a rock climbing wall), a motion-capture studio, a cafe, catering space, and a private exterior patio.
While the brochure didn't directly identify the studio, a statement provided to press verified that Bungie was actively pursuing a sublease.
"Bungie is exploring options to sublease its campus in Bellevue, Washington. The studio transitioned to a digital-first model several years ago, and this move reflects the team's evolving workplace needs and the effectiveness of its remote collaboration," Bungie said. "Bungie will continue to maintain a physical office presence in Bellevue."
Bungie formally adopted remote work eligibility for most of its roles in 2022, following the studio's shift to work-from-home development during the COVID-19 lockdown years—effectively defeating the purpose of its office expansion due to circumstances that would have been impossible to predict during its early planning stages.
Bungie wasn't the only games company to make ill-fated investments during the height of the pandemic: Analysts have repeatedly cited overly-ambitious expansions and acquisitions—propelled by the COVID era's low interests rates and explosion of at-home entertainment revenue—as one of the driving forces behind the games industry's brutal cost-cutting in the years that followed.
Bungie's overextension, however, was particularly drastic. After Sony purchased the studio for $3.6 billion in 2022 , Bungie leadership embarked on a rampant hiring spree, adding hundreds of developers to the payroll to fill out development teams for a swath of simultaneous incubation projects—projects that would prove unsustainable as the impact of Covid waned and revenues started to tumble across the industry.
A mass layoff followed in October 2023 , affecting roughly 100 employees. The next round cut 220 developers in July 2024 as fallout from Bungie leadership having reportedly "overstated their studio’s financial prospects to Sony," leading to a dire enough fiscal outlook that even the success of Destiny 2's Final Shape expansion couldn't salvage it. As Sony intensified its oversight amidst the mounting turmoil, Bungie's leadership began to abandon ship, culminating with Pete Parsons departing the studio in 2025—presumably in one of his vintage collector cars .
Bungie staff ultimately suffered another sweeping layoff in June 2026, with most of the Destiny team losing their jobs in the aftermath of Destiny 2's end of live service. At peak employment, Bungie's staff numbered over 1,600; in July 2024, Parsons said the studio numbered around 850 . The WARN notice issued for this June's layoff indicated at least 292 jobs were affected.
In other words, if all of Bungie's remaining employees gathered in its office, there would be fewer than 600 people to fill its 211,000 square feet.
If you're interested, the master lease runs through September 30, 2035.

title: 'Grand Theft Auto is a videogame franchise built around criminal activity': Miami-Dade County Sheriff comes out hard against a proposed GTA 6 collab with Rockstar
author: Andy Chalk
text:
Officials with Miami-Dade County have held talks with Rockstar about using facilities and landmarks in the county to promote the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 , according to a recent report by The Miamian , saying it could represent "a unique opportunity to generate revenue for the County while showcasing Miami-Dade to a massive audience." Just one problem: the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office is dead-set against it.
The Miamian report (via RPS ) says the county submitted a pitch deck to Rockstar on June 29, after which staff had "some conversations with Rockstar about potential opportunities around the launch of GTA 6," said Carlos Suarez, a spokesperson for Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava.
"Nothing has been formally agreed to or approved, and any idea would have to go through the appropriate review and approval process," Suarez said. "Given Miami-Dade's clear influence on the game, we think there could be a unique opportunity to generate revenue for the County while showcasing Miami-Dade to a massive audience."
Miami-Dade is the inspiration for Vice City in the GTA series, and by "inspiration" I mean it basically is Vice City, although Miami exists as a separate city in the game's fiction. Vice City will serve as a central location in GTA 6, and will represent the seat of Vice-Dale County, much as the city of Miami is the county seat of Miami-Dade. Given that, the campaign makes obvious sense, and most of the ideas floated don't sound too overly disruptive.
Some examples:
A display aircraft wrapped in Vice City logos and a GTA 6-inspired baggage claim at Miami International Airport
Vice City signage and colors at the Metromover and Metrorail transit stations
Vice City-inspired installations or public art at PortMiami
A "family appropriate" celebration of "Miami car culture" with cars, bikes, DJs, food, artists, and branded installations at Tropical Park
A Vice City Radio Lab at the city's main library, providing access to recording, editing, and digital media equipment to support "music production, podcasting, oral histories, neighborhood storytelling, sound engineering, video-game development, and other creative programming, while reflecting the central role that music and radio play in the GTA experience
The pitch also includes ideas for Rockstar funding permanent upgrades to county infrastructure:
(Image credit: Miami-Dade County) That all sounds pretty cool to me, and some of it is quite civically wholesome, too. Yes, it's all part of the monstrous marketing machine for the biggest videogame of all time, but it also seems like the county is coming at it as a way to celebrate the real people and civic culture that led Rockstar to embrace Miami in the first place, and that counts for something.
The big stumbling block, of course, is that the GTA games are the polar opposite of civic-minded and wholesome, and that's led Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz to speak out against the idea.
"Grand Theft Auto is a videogame franchise built around criminal activity," Cordero-Stutz told the Miami Herald . "Its fictional world includes murder, robbery, drug trafficking, carjacking, violence against law enforcement, and other conduct that the men and women of the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office work every single day to prevent."
Miami-Dade Commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez also spoke out against the idea: "We should be promoting the Miami-Dade we have worked so hard to build, not a fictional version of our community defined by crime and violence."
The sheriff isn't wrong. GTA games have always been notoriously violent: Former attorney Jack Thompson , at one time the videogame industry's foremost nemesis, spent years campaigning hard against the games and publisher Take-Two Interactive before he was finally disbarred for his relentless antics and misconduct.
But the game industry, and its audience, have matured in the 25 years (that's right, look it up) since Grand Theft Auto 3 changed everything: GTA is still steeped in criminal violence, but the shock factor—and the hand-wringing over it—are long gone. These days it's completely mainstream, as evidenced by the performance of the GTA 6 reveal showcase on Netflix, which was the platform's biggest show of the week.
Would Miami-Dade have to tone down some of the seedier elements of GTA 6 for its "family appropriate" events? Sure. But I also have no doubt that a significant number of sheriff's deputies and police in the county grew up playing GTA themselves, and I bet an awful lot of them will be calling in sick when GTA 6 drops.

Miami-Dade Commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez also spoke out against the idea: "We should be promoting the Miami-Dade we have worked so hard to build, not a fictional version of our community defined by crime and violence."

The sheriff isn't wrong. GTA games have always been notoriously violent: Former attorney Jack Thompson, at one time the videogame industry's foremost nemesis, spent years campaigning hard against the games and publisher Take-Two Interactive before he was finally disbarred for his relentless antics and misconduct.

But the game industry, and its audience, have matured in the 25 years (that's right, look it up) since Grand Theft Auto 3 changed everything: GTA is still steeped in criminal violence, but the shock factor—and the hand-wringing over it—are long gone. These days it's completely mainstream, as evidenced by the performance of the GTA 6 reveal showcase on Netflix, which was the platform's biggest show of the week.

Would Miami-Dade have to tone down some of the seedier elements of GTA 6 for its "family appropriate" events? Sure. But I also have no doubt that a significant number of sheriff's deputies and police in the county grew up playing GTA themselves, and I bet an awful lot of them will be calling in sick when GTA 6 drops.

title: Celebrate Labor Day by playing Civilization 7 for free
author: Andy Chalk
text:
The Labor Day weekend is upon us (in Canada and the US, anyway, and we'll be sure to spare a thought for our UK colleagues who will be working on Monday) and holy cow, it is about time. If you find yourself in need of something to do, here's a thought: Play Civilization 7, because it's free to play on Steam until September 10.
Civ 7's had kind of a rough go of things since it launched in early 2025. It made some big changes to the formula that didn't go over well with a significant portion of the fan base, the UI was almost universally unpopular, and performance was dodgy.
Firaxis has been banging away on it ever since, to mixed results: A major update released in May brought a big bump in player numbers on Steam, but the reactions expressed via Steam reviews were almost literally split down the middle. Civ 7's Steam rating remains "mixed," with only 48% positive user reviews, while concurrent player numbers on the platform are still running neck-and-neck with the 16-year-old Civilization 5.
Civ 5 is much beloved but I imagine Firaxis and Take-Two would like to see people move on.
(Image credit: SteamDB) Ah, but here's the counterpoint: It's free . Just go around to Steam and click the "Play Game" button, and after some requisite amount of downloading, you're playing Civ 7 without spending a penny . It's hard to go wrong, really.
If the past year-and-a-half of updates have got Civilization 7 to a point where you think to yourself, 'Yes, I would like to play this game all the time,' you can also pick up the standard and deluxe editions for half price until September 17: That's $35/£30/€35 for the former, and $50/£45/€50 for the latter.
The Civ 7 development team (a small part of it, anyway) will also be discussing what comes next during a livestream from PAX on September 5—you can catch that on YouTube , Twitch , and Facebook .

title: As Wardogs blows past 200k Steam concurrents, its developers are prepared for the day 'hype dies down'
author: Morgan Park
text:
The way our hobby talks about player counts is all sorts of messed up. Steam concurrents are a useful metric for gauging a game's general popularity, but they paint an incomplete picture. They're a single data point, yet have become the flimsy scaffolding on which the internet builds elaborate headcanon about a game's quality, viability, or deadness. Sometimes dogpiling is so successful, and the resulting perception so difficult to fight, that simply saying a game is dead is enough to help kill it.
It's a trend that annoys me to no end, so it's refreshing to see a developer speaking openly about concurrents—both about how many it considers "healthy," and why it's normal for the number to rise and fall. It's been a recurring topic for Wardogs developer Bulkhead, whose closed beta surpassed 200,000 concurrents today on Steam. Responding to a TimTheTatman clip on X, CEO Joe Brammer spoke on the milsim's unexpected popularity, and its inevitable (but healthy) decline.
"Wardogs will continue to lose players for months as the hype dies down," Brammer wrote . "Doesn't make it a bad game or even a problem, we planned for 5k players concurrent! It'll maintain a healthy playerbase and we'll continue to build the 1.0 version of the game then... it'll boom again :) And so the cycle continues :)"
It's a cycle many of us are familiar with, but rarely acknowledge. I tend to build a rotation of multiplayer favorites that I regularly return to, either to check out an update or scratch an itch. It is, I think, a pretty healthy way to enjoy videogames, but the rise of live service "forever" games, as well as high-profile failures, have proliferated the idea that videogames are those species of shark that will die if they ever stop swimming.
(Image credit: Joe Brammer on X) Much like the majority of videogames before 2016, Bulkhead does not need Wardogs to be a consistent, top-charting megahit to continue making it. In a video published last month outlining " 10 reasons not to buy Wardogs ," game director Howard Philpott expanded on Bulkhead's expectations:
"We expect our initial days after launch to have a lot more players than expected, but we can tell you for a fact that this is completely normal. Those players will fall away over the next coming months. Player numbers will drop off, and journalists and influencers on the fringe of the community will try to ragebait your enjoyment out of the game for social media clicks. This doesn't mean the game is dying. We're thinking longer term than a flash in the plan. Our goal is to settle into a sustainable, close-knit community. If we're pulling in 3,000 to 5,000 daily concurrent players who genuinely love the game, it'll allow new players to buy in anytime and join an active community."
If we put our hands together on this one, we can all be normal about a multiplayer shooter. Wardogs is out September 10, but pre-ordering grants access to the closed beta ending Sunday.

title: September's schedule of new games, events, and updates refuses to let 2026 go down in history as a slow year for new releases
author: Andrea Shearon
text:
After a quiet few months, September finally hits the gas, and our list of monthly PC game happenings is filled with brand new adventures, series continuations, 1.0 updates, and events galore. I'm still playing catch-up after Gamescom, and now we've got Tokyo Game Show queued up soon. It's the same schedule every year, but somehow I'm always caught off guard.
The Blood of Dawnwalker kicked off the month with a delightfully dismal vampire RPG from the Witcher veterans at Rebel Wolves. Then you've got all month to suck blood as Coen (or be a good two-shoes and abstain, I guess) before Silent Hill: Townfall and Control Resonant launch on the same damn day. It seems everything I've been waiting all year to play has crammed into this 4-week window, and that's not even counting all the big updates.
The Witcher 3 Remastered is easily among the most notable updates, and everyone who owns the original gets the RPG's makeover for free (along with its DLC). It'll be my first time playing, so between that and Valheim 1.0, I'll be plenty busy until 2027.
September 2026 PC Gamer highlights
September 2
The Blood of Dawnwalker
Steam | I've been loving The Blood of Dawnwalker, but you don't have to take my broody, vampire-obsessed word for it. Shaun called it "one of best action RPGs [he's] played in years," in his Blood of Dawnwalker review .
September 24
Silent Hill: Townfall
Steam | I have to say it every time: I still can't believe we're in a Silent Hill renaissance. I'm hoping Townfall continues this trend of one banger release after another, and from how Fraser explains his time as Simon in a hellish version of Scotland, it has a chance.
September 24
Control Resonant
Steam | After years of insisting I would not like Control's gameplay, I finally beat it last month and ate crow. As it turns out, I'm full of it, and I love everything about Control. While I am a little worried about Dylan's melee brawling, I've learned my lesson and will give little brother Faden a fair shot later this month.
September 29
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered
Steam | The Witcher 3 is another RPG I'm late to the party for, but in my defense, it has a very good and very distracting card game. I don't know how many times I've booted up Geralt's adventure only to play Gwent for ten hours before stopping, but this seems like a good opportunity to break the cycle.

title: Left 4 Dead 2 writer says Valve intentionally 'leaked' its cinematic trailer to get around ESRB rules: 'I think we can't get trouble for that now'
author: Rick Lane
text:
It's strange to think about in hindsight, but Left 4 Dead 2 was a controversial game in the run-up to its release in November 2009—just one year after the original Left 4 Dead laid the foundations for today's enormous cooperative gaming scene. Indeed, it was that rapid turnaround, combined with the fact that the first Left 4 Dead was a relatively short game, which led to accusations that Left 4 Dead 2 was nothing more than a cynical ploy by Valve to cash in on the success of the first.
Ultimately, Left 4 Dead 2 would prove a worthy follow-up to Valve's cooperative blaster. But it turns out there was some skulduggery afoot behind the scenes on Left 4 Dead 2, just not the kind that fans suspected. Shortly before the sequel's launch, a cinematic trailer—which would ultimately serve as Left 4 Dead 2's introductory cutscene—leaked onto the Internet. Now, it's been revealed that this 'leak' was orchestrated by Valve to evade the censorious watch of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board.
This is according to former Valve writer and Left 4 Dead designer Chet Faliszek, who revealed Valve's deliberate leak in a YouTube video about cut Left 4 Dead voice lines (via Ars Technica ). In the video, Faliszek explains why Left 4 Dead 2 had a large number of voice lines cut from the final game. One reason was that, at the time, Valve had run-ins with numerous countries and ratings boards over the series' depictions of violence and use of profane language.
"You have to remember, especially during Left 4 Dead 1 and Left 4 Dead 2 time, Valve was in fights with the ESRB, with Australia, with Germany, with a bunch of countries about the profanity in the game, or the violence," he explains. "One of [Valve's] lawyers stepped in and said that us writers needed to be babysat on this. And so [the] first thing we did was, well, we made sure there was no profanity in there that crosses the line—basically F-bombs."
Faliszek personally believed that, when it comes to censorship of language and depictions of violence, "you push it and have the ESRB push back". But Valve's lawyer felt differently and Faliszek went along with it. However, the ESRB's regulatory oversight didn't just cover games, but extended to the marketing material for those games. And unlike today, the ESRB had different regulatory rules for trailers and games. Language or violence that might land a game a 'Mature' rating could result in a trailer that depicted the same things being banned outright.
It's this exact scenario Valve faced with Left 4 Dead 2. The cinematic trailer is no more violent or foul-mouthed than the game itself, but according to Faliszek, the ESRB drew a hard line on it. Hence, Valve decided the trailer should find its way online by 'accident'. "We leaked our trailer ahead of time, because they wouldn't let us release the trailer," Faliszek says. "I'll just admit that. I think we can't get in trouble for that now. It's like 20 years ago."

It's strange to think about in hindsight, but Left 4 Dead 2 was a controversial game in the run-up to its release in November 2009—just one year after the original Left 4 Dead laid the foundations for today's enormous cooperative gaming scene. Indeed, it was that rapid turnaround, combined with the fact that the first Left 4 Dead was a relatively short game, which led to accusations that Left 4 Dead 2 was nothing more than a cynical ploy by Valve to cash in on the success of the first.

Ultimately, Left 4 Dead 2 would prove a worthy follow-up to Valve's cooperative blaster. But it turns out there was some skulduggery afoot behind the scenes on Left 4 Dead 2, just not the kind that fans suspected. Shortly before the sequel's launch, a cinematic trailer—which would ultimately serve as Left 4 Dead 2's introductory cutscene—leaked onto the Internet. Now, it's been revealed that this 'leak' was orchestrated by Valve to evade the censorious watch of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board.

This is according to former Valve writer and Left 4 Dead designer Chet Faliszek, who revealed Valve's deliberate leak in a YouTube video about cut Left 4 Dead voice lines (via Ars Technica). In the video, Faliszek explains why Left 4 Dead 2 had a large number of voice lines cut from the final game. One reason was that, at the time, Valve had run-ins with numerous countries and ratings boards over the series' depictions of violence and use of profane language.

"You have to remember, especially during Left 4 Dead 1 and Left 4 Dead 2 time, Valve was in fights with the ESRB, with Australia, with Germany, with a bunch of countries about the profanity in the game, or the violence," he explains. "One of [Valve's] lawyers stepped in and said that us writers needed to be babysat on this. And so [the] first thing we did was, well, we made sure there was no profanity in there that crosses the line—basically F-bombs."

Faliszek personally believed that, when it comes to censorship of language and depictions of violence, "you push it and have the ESRB push back". But Valve's lawyer felt differently and Faliszek went along with it. However, the ESRB's regulatory oversight didn't just cover games, but extended to the marketing material for those games. And unlike today, the ESRB had different regulatory rules for trailers and games. Language or violence that might land a game a 'Mature' rating could result in a trailer that depicted the same things being banned outright.

It's this exact scenario Valve faced with Left 4 Dead 2. The cinematic trailer is no more violent or foul-mouthed than the game itself, but according to Faliszek, the ESRB drew a hard line on it. Hence, Valve decided the trailer should find its way online by 'accident'. "We leaked our trailer ahead of time, because they wouldn't let us release the trailer," Faliszek says. "I'll just admit that. I think we can't get in trouble for that now. It's like 20 years ago."
